transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya, Jamal (Redwood); Lena, Samir, Priya (Riverstone)

Summary (auto): Discussed contract extension mechanics, incremental capacity (dedicated vs hosted), EU edge provisioning timeline, and compliance docs. Action owners assigned.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh, we'll keep this tight — agenda is renewal terms, capacity bump, eu-edge onboarding, and any red lines from procurement.
[00:18] Lena: thanks Maya, quick context — we've been running ~40M tokens/month today, peak QPS around 120 for search re-ranker, want to plan for 3x headroom for holiday season.
[00:32] Samir: and key for us is that eu traffic must stay in eu-west region — data residency, and we'd like a private VPC path into the dedicated pool if possible.
[00:47] Jamal: got it. from a tech lens we can do eu-edge provision — private deployment or dedicated capacity with VPC peering. slight note, private on-prem is heavier lift; dedicated in-region usually hits latency SLOs.
[01:05] Priya: procurement here — timeline: need PO within four weeks, legal wants a clause for audit logs and KMS integration; do you support HSM-backed keys?
[01:20] Maya: yes, we support KMS integrations and can outline HSM options — I'll add that to the security packet we send.
[01:29] Lena: can you share the SOC2 report? last time the link expired.
[01:34] Jamal: yeah, will re-share SOC2 and the network topology diagram — note sometimes the doc name gets munged, so I'll include the exact paths.
[01:50] Samir: on latency — our upper bound is 120ms median for the re-ranker from eu users, is that realistic on a shared hosted tier?
[02:02] Jamal: on hosted, you might see mid-100s depending on batching; for consistent 120ms median we recommend dedicated eu capacity or our eu-edge node — that reduces tail latency and gives predictable KV cache warm states.
[02:25] Lena: what's the approximate commit for dedicated? we were thinking about a stepped approach: start with 2x current, then add burst capacity for traffic surges.
[02:36] Maya: commercial model would be base reserved capacity plus a burst bucket for seasonal uplift. for numbers, we can propose a base that covers 80% of expected daily tokens and a burst that auto-scales up to 3x for short windows.
[02:54] Priya: ok, question — on billing, can burst be billed daily vs monthly? our finance prefers usage-based for bursts.
[03:04] Maya: yes, burst is usage-billed; reserved is committed monthly/annual. we'll show both options in the updated quote.
[03:12] Samir: technical follow-up: how do you handle KV cache warm-start on new nodes? last pilot had a cold-start hit that spiked latency.
[03:25] Jamal: good call — we do prefix and KV caching with a reprovisioning policy, and we can pin certain models to nodes for warm caches. cold-starts are mitigated with pre-warming scripts during scale events. we should test this in the 48-hour pilot.
[03:44] Lena: we also have compliance around redaction — logs leaving the VPC need to be redacted. is there an option to filter traces?
[03:54] Jamal: yes, we support token-level redaction rules and configurable audit log retention; still need to confirm the retention window you want.
[04:06] Priya: legal will request an SLA that includes availability and latency targets, also a clause around incident notifications. what SLAs do you typically offer for Dedicated?
[04:18] Maya: Dedicated comes with an uptime SLA (99.9) and latency targets per model class; we can pull the service spec into the quote appendix.
[04:30] Samir: do you have regional failover? if eu-west goes down, does traffic route to us-east? we need a failover plan that doesn't breach residency rules.
[04:42] Jamal: routing policies are configurable — we can failover to a compatible eu region or a limited fallback mode that strips PII and routes to a non-resident region only under explicit triggered conditions. that's part of the routing policy we can lock down.
[05:00] Lena: Great. can you also confirm which model variants you'll deploy in eu? we need deterministic behavior vs the hosted latest model drift.
[05:11] Jamal: customers can pin model versions; we recommend pinning to the validated quantized variant for production. Redwood's model catalog will list the model id; we'll include the exact model identifiers in the readout.
[05:28] Priya: procurement redline — we need export controls language and an indemnity cap. can legal team review the standard T&Cs quickly?
[05:40] Maya: yes, we'll push a contract redline window and propose minor adjustments; expect a redline doc with highlights.
[05:48] Samir: are there any competitors that offer a cheaper burst? we've been talking to a couple — Anthropic and some self-hosted teams. main question is cost vs ops overhead.
[06:00] Maya: totally — Anthropic and OpenAI options are often simple per-request but can be more expensive at scale; in-house k8s reduces per-token cost but ops are heavy. our value is predictable economics and operational tooling to keep unit cost low.
[06:18] Lena: ok, technical nit — do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for team-level keys? we want strict role separation for production keys.
[06:28] Jamal: yes SAML and fine-grained RBAC; we can demo the RBAC policy model in Console and show token scoping.
[06:38] Priya: timeline recap from our side: procurement needs final quote by Sep 15, legal sign-off by Sep 22, target go-live before Black Friday.
[06:51] Maya: understood — that aligns with our operations if we do the 2-week EU edge prep and then the 48-hour pilot in the last week of August / first week of September.
[07:03] Samir: for the pilot, what metrics will you provide? we need latency percentiles, error rates, and token counts plus a cost projection.
[07:13] Jamal: we'll deliver p50/p95/p99 latency, qps, token consumption, and a cost model estimate with sensitivity analysis.
[07:22] Lena: any risk items? list them out.
[07:26] Jamal: big ones: KV cache cold starts, model quantization regressions for rare prompts, and network egress misconfigurations. each has mitigations: pre-warming, eval suite, and pre-flight network test.
[07:40] Priya: ok, finance — can you give a sample amortization over the contract? we may prefer a 12-month term with quarterly review.
[07:50] Maya: yes, quote will include both 12-month amortized and monthly-billed options.
[07:56] Lena: on the EU edge provisioning, is a dedicated GPU pool required or can you use dedicated slices on shared hardware?
[08:07] Jamal: we have both options — reserved GPU pools (full nodes) are best for predictable latency; shared slices can work for cost efficiency but reduce tail predictability.
[08:20] Samir: we'd prefer reserved pools for re-ranking.
[08:24] Maya: noted.
[08:28] Lena: anything else from Redwood?
[08:30] Jamal: I'll attach the network diagram, SOC2, and the pre-warm runbook.
[08:35] Maya: and I'll revise the quote with explicit burst terms and pricing tiers.
[08:39] Priya: we'll circulate internal sign-off calendar and confirm PO template.
[08:43] Lena: ok, sounds actionable. let's recap next steps.
[08:47] Maya: recap: Maya sends updated quote + appendix by 2026-08-25; Jamal sends SOC2, network diagram, pre-warm runbook by 2026-08-24; Jamal & Samir schedule 48h EU-edge pilot week of 2026-08-31; Priya to share PO constraints by 2026-08-26.
[09:06] Priya: yep. thanks everyone.
[09:09] Maya: thanks team, we'll follow up in email with attachments. bye.

Notes: frequent minor transcription errors: 'k v cache' sometimes as 'kay vee cache', 'Redwood Console' heard as 'red wood console', SAML spelled 'S A M L' occasionally. Links referenced: security packet (link to internal Redwood S3) — to be attached after call.

End of transcript.
